The background jobs died again since the sandbox seems to kill the whole process tree on session interruptions, so setsid isn't surviving. I need to design experiments that either finish within a single tool call's time limit or rely on the Bash tool's run_in_background feature instead.

Looking at my synthetic scale results, forward correction is clearly helping — noise_rate around 0.35-0.4 with weight decay 0.1-0.3 gives the best accuracy, roughly a 1.2-1.5% gain over baseline. Next I want to finish the end-to-end run on the 80k synthetic set with a tight timeout, and improve the ensemble rule so it only averages models within a tolerance of the best performer, requiring a minimum gain margin before including them — I'm now working out how to define that margin relative to standard error.

Detached jobs keep dying with the session, so I'll run each experiment in a single call going forward. Partial results confirm forward noise correction helps (0.964 vs 0.952), so next I'll refine the ensembling rule and run the full synthetic production test in one call.
